beats.label: S1 · Wrong car
beats.text: Jimmy tries to poach the Kettlemans with a staged accident; his hires hit the wrong car and pull him into Tuco Salamanca's orbit at gunpoint.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First contact with the cartel world Jimmy will keep circling back into.

beats.label: S1 · In the game
beats.text: Nacho, watching Jimmy talk Tuco down, offers to steal the Kettlemans' embezzled cash and tells him to call when he's 'in the game'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the Jimmy–Nacho line that reroutes both their lives.

beats.label: S1 · The right thing
beats.text: Jimmy tracks the Kettlemans hiding with the cash; with Mike he takes it back and forces Craig into a plea, choosing the right thing over the money.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the choice Jimmy will spend the rest of the season regretting.

beats.label: S1 · Sandpiper
beats.text: A billboard stunt against HHM brings Jimmy elder clients, and at Sandpiper Crossing he finds a fraud too big to run alone — he brings it to Chuck.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sandpiper becomes the payday and pressure point driving Jimmy for years.

beats.label: S1 · Chuck's line
beats.text: Chuck breaks his EHS to phone Howard and cut Jimmy out of the case, admitting he never wanted Jimmy to be a lawyer at all.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The betrayal that sets the McGill feud engine for the whole series.

beats.label: S1 · Never again
beats.text: A week of Cicero cons with Marco ends when Marco dies mid-con; Jimmy skips his Davis & Main offer and tells Mike he won't do the right thing again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The verbal commitment that turns Jimmy toward Saul.

cliffhanger.text: Jimmy has walked away from his one shot at legitimacy and told Mike he's done doing the right thing. Chuck, whose contempt he now sees clearly, is still the name partner in a firm that will keep freezing him out.
questions: Does Jimmy actually turn down Davis & Main, or come back for it?
How does Jimmy square his new outlook with Kim, who's still betting on HHM?
Now that Jimmy knows Chuck sabotaged him, what does the McGill feud become?

characters.name: Jimmy McGill
characters.line: A hustling public defender working out of a nail salon back room, chasing a big case at Sandpiper Crossing after swearing off cons following Marco's death.

characters.name: Chuck McGill
characters.line: Jimmy's older brother and a founding partner at HHM, housebound with electromagnetic hypersensitivity, who has quietly worked to keep Jimmy out of the law.

characters.name: The Kettlemans
characters.line: A county treasurer and his wife who embezzled $1.6M and, after Jimmy recovered the cash, took a plea deal for Craig.

characters.name: Tuco Salamanca
characters.line: A volatile Salamanca enforcer whose desert standoff with Jimmy first pulled him into the cartel's orbit.

characters.name: Nacho Varga
characters.line: Tuco's calmer lieutenant, intrigued by Jimmy's talk-down of Tuco and waiting for the day he calls to get 'in the game'.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: A retired Philadelphia cop working the courthouse parking booth who helped Jimmy retrieve the Kettleman money without keeping a cent.

characters.name: Howard Hamlin
characters.line: The polished managing partner at HHM who fronts Chuck's refusals to hire Jimmy, taking the heat Chuck won't.

beats.label: S2 · Bad fit
beats.text: Jimmy joins Davis & Main, hates the suit, and airs an unapproved TV ad that puts Kim in the line of fire back at HHM.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the mutual sabotage-by-Slippin'-Jimmy that will detonate both their firm positions.

beats.label: S2 · Kim's Mesa Verde
beats.text: Kim lands Mesa Verde on her own but Howard keeps her in document review; she cons a mark with Jimmy and starts imagining a life outside HHM.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kim's first taste of leaving; the client that will define her career and Jimmy's next move.

beats.label: S2 · Wexler-McGill
beats.text: Both walk: Jimmy engineers his own firing to keep his signing bonus, Kim leaves with Mesa Verde, and they share a converted dentists' office.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the shared practice and the entangled finances that drive the season's crime.

beats.label: S2 · Doctored pages
beats.text: Chuck sinks Kim's Mesa Verde pitch with faint praise; Jimmy retaliates by swapping page numbers in Chuck's filing so the bank runs back to Kim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The felony at the center of the season — the one Chuck will spend everything to prove.

beats.label: S2 · Working for Hector
beats.text: Mike goads Tuco into a beating that jails him, then takes $50,000 from Hector Salamanca to lie that the gun was his — his first paid job for the family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Mike is now on Hector's payroll and inside the Salamancas' reach, setting up the truck job that follows.

beats.label: S2 · Don't
beats.text: Mike ambushes a Salamanca truck for $250,000; when he lines up a rifle shot on Hector, a car horn and a note reading 'Don't' stop him cold.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the invisible hand — the season-defining question Mike will chase into next season.

beats.label: S2 · The tape
beats.text: Chuck stages a fall at the copy store to lure Jimmy into confessing to the tampering — and secretly records every word.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The evidence Chuck will weaponize; the trap Jimmy is walking into blind.

cliffhanger.text: Chuck has Jimmy on tape admitting to a felony he thinks was a private moment of comfort. Mike, aiming at Hector to end the Salamanca problem, has just been silently overruled by someone else in the game.
questions: How does Chuck plan to use a confession Jimmy doesn't know exists?
Who is watching Mike, and why do they want Hector alive?
Can Kim and Jimmy's shared practice — built on the Mesa Verde swap — survive what Chuck knows?

characters.name: Jimmy McGill
characters.line: Briefly an associate at Davis & Main, he engineers his own firing to keep the bonus and quietly tampers with Chuck's Mesa Verde filing.

characters.name: Kim Wexler
characters.line: An HHM associate who lands Mesa Verde on her own, is punished with doc review, and leaves to share a two-office practice with Jimmy.

characters.name: Chuck McGill
characters.line: Convinced Jimmy sabotaged his Mesa Verde work, he stages a copy-store fall to draw a taped confession out of his brother.

characters.name: Howard Hamlin
characters.line: HHM's managing partner, who kept Kim on document review after Mesa Verde and now finds himself losing that client to her.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: Drawn deeper into cartel work, he takes $50K from Hector to eat Tuco's gun charge, then aborts a rifle shot on Hector after an anonymous 'Don't' note.

characters.name: Hector Salamanca
characters.line: The Salamanca family's regional boss, now paying Mike to bury Tuco's assault charge and using his ice-cream trucks to move product.

characters.name: Mesa Verde
characters.line: The regional bank whose expansion work Kim wins, loses to Chuck's HHM, and reclaims after Jimmy's filing swap.

beats.label: S3 · Los Pollos
beats.text: Mike tails his mystery surveillance to Los Pollos Hermanos; manager Gus Fring meets him with a deal — don't kill Hector, help disrupt him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Gus and locks Mike into his orbit, the pivot that reshapes everyone's storyline going forward.

beats.label: S3 · The trap
beats.text: Chuck plays Jimmy's confession for Howard and a hired PI, then baits Jimmy into breaking in to destroy the tape while witnesses watch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The move that turns the McGill feud into an official proceeding.

beats.label: S3 · Chicanery
beats.text: At Jimmy's bar hearing, Kim plants Chuck's phone battery on him; Chuck's rant on the stand exposes his EHS as psychological and finishes his career.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The public destruction of Chuck — the wound that drives him into his last months.

beats.label: S3 · Saul is born
beats.text: Jimmy's one-year law suspension births 'Saul Goodman' hustling TV airtime; Kim, covering everything alone, burns out and totals her car.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The alias appears for the first time as a business, and Kim's collapse sets up her retreat next season.

beats.label: S3 · The pill swap
beats.text: Nacho, sick of Hector's threats against his father, swaps Hector's nitro for placebos; Hector strokes at a meeting with Gus, and Gus lets him live.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Hector as a functioning boss and hands Gus a permanent hook into Nacho.

beats.label: S3 · Chuck alone
beats.text: Chuck is forced out of HHM and turns his EHS on his own house; Jimmy comes to make peace, and Chuck refuses him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The last brotherly conversation, and the moment Jimmy's guilt is locked in.

beats.label: S3 · Lantern
beats.text: Jimmy sabotages his own Sandpiper payday to rehabilitate Irene. That night Chuck knocks over a lantern and burns his house down with himself inside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's twin acts of self-destruction — the fire is the psychic center of everything that follows.

cliffhanger.text: Chuck has just killed himself, and only Jimmy will understand his own share of the blame. Gus now quietly owns Nacho, and a bedridden Hector has been left alive for a reason nobody outside Gus's head knows.
questions: How does Jimmy carry — or refuse to carry — the guilt of Chuck's death?
What is Gus building with the pieces of Hector's operation?
With Kim recovering and Jimmy suspended, what is left of their practice together?

characters.name: Jimmy McGill
characters.line: Suspended from law for a year after Chuck's tape, he reinvents himself hawking commercial airtime as 'Saul Goodman' and torpedoes his own Sandpiper payday to help Irene.

characters.name: Chuck McGill
characters.line: Broken on the stand at Jimmy's bar hearing and forced out of HHM, he relapses into full EHS and dies when a lantern topples in his gutted house.

characters.name: Kim Wexler
characters.line: Jimmy's partner and lover, carrying Mesa Verde and every other client alone until she totals her car from exhaustion.

characters.name: Howard Hamlin
characters.line: HHM's managing partner, who pays out Chuck's buyout personally to force him into retirement.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: Now openly working for Gus, tailing his own surveillance to Los Pollos Hermanos and accepting a role in disrupting the Salamancas.

characters.name: Gus Fring
characters.line: The Los Pollos Hermanos owner and secret cartel distributor, who recruits Mike, tolerates Nacho's pill swap, and keeps Hector alive in a wheelchair to prolong his suffering.

characters.name: Nacho Varga
characters.line: Terrified for his father, he swaps Hector's nitro pills for placebos and triggers the stroke at Don Eladio's summit.

characters.name: Hector Salamanca
characters.line: The Salamanca boss whose meeting with Gus ends in the stroke that will leave him mute and wheelchair-bound.

beats.label: S4 · Eerily fine
beats.text: Chuck's death is ruled an accident; Jimmy lets Howard take the blame and comes back from the funeral eerily fine, while Kim rages at Howard on his behalf.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the lie at the center of Jimmy and Kim's marriage-to-be — she's fighting Chuck's ghost blind.

beats.label: S4 · Hector's cage
beats.text: Gus quietly nurses Hector through his stroke, then dismisses the doctor mid-recovery, trapping Hector's mind inside a body that cannot speak.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The choice that keeps Hector alive as a symbol of Gus's revenge, feeding every Salamanca move to come.

beats.label: S4 · Gus owns Nacho
beats.text: Nacho becomes Gus's mole: after Arturo is killed and Nacho is shot in a staged attack, Gus tells him he knows about the pill swap and now owns him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nacho's position for the rest of the series — the inside man who cannot leave.

beats.label: S4 · Schweikart
beats.text: Kim joins Schweikart & Cokely so she can keep Mesa Verde and take pro bono defense work; over months she thrives, and she and Jimmy quietly drift.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kim's career finds its shape while Jimmy's leaves the room — the gap that lets Saul be born unopposed.

beats.label: S4 · The lab
beats.text: Mike takes a Madrigal security cover and, under Gus, oversees German engineer Werner Ziegler secretly excavating the underground meth lab.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The lab that will drive the cartel plot into next season begins to exist.

beats.label: S4 · Lalo arrives, Werner dies
beats.text: Werner slips away to see his wife; Lalo Salamanca — Hector's charming nephew, freshly arrived — tricks lab details out of him, and Mike is ordered to shoot Werner.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the next season's antagonist and the wound that reshapes Mike's loyalty to Gus.

beats.label: S4 · Saul Goodman, s'all good
beats.text: Jimmy fakes remorse for Chuck to win reinstatement, then tells Kim he will practice as 'Saul Goodman' — an announcement that stops her cold.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment the alias becomes the man; the shock Kim will still be metabolizing next season.

cliffhanger.text: Jimmy has legally become 'Saul Goodman', and Kim just realized the man she loves has replaced himself with an alias. Lalo Salamanca has arrived in Albuquerque already suspicious of Werner's death and everything around Gus's operation.
questions: How much of Jimmy is left inside Saul Goodman?
What will Lalo see when he starts pulling on the threads of Gus's operation?
Can Kim keep working alongside a man who no longer wants his own name?

characters.name: Jimmy McGill
characters.line: Numb after Chuck's death, he fakes remorse to win reinstatement and announces to Kim that he'll practice under 'Saul Goodman'.

characters.name: Kim Wexler
characters.line: Now at Schweikart & Cokely with Mesa Verde in tow, she throws herself into pro bono defense work and is blindsided by Jimmy's Saul plan.

characters.name: Chuck McGill
characters.line: Dead by suicide before the season begins, his ruling as accidental lets Jimmy shed blame while Kim rages at Howard on his behalf.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: Working a Madrigal security cover for Gus, he oversees Werner's dig and is forced to shoot the engineer when he goes off-leash.

characters.name: Gus Fring
characters.line: Building the superlab under a laundry, he keeps Hector alive as a puppet and installs Nacho as his mole inside the Salamancas.

characters.name: Werner Ziegler
characters.line: The German engineer secretly excavating Gus's lab, whose homesick slip to Lalo costs him his life at Mike's hand.

characters.name: Lalo Salamanca
characters.line: Hector's charming, dangerous nephew freshly arrived to run family business, already sniffing around Werner and Gus's operation.

characters.name: Nacho Varga
characters.line: Wounded in a staged attack that killed Arturo, he is now owned by Gus, who knows about the pill swap.

characters.name: Hector Salamanca
characters.line: Nursed back to twitching consciousness by Gus, trapped in a body that can barely tap a bell.

beats.label: S5 · Lalo's lawyer
beats.text: Jimmy hangs the Saul Goodman shingle; Nacho, forced by Gus, delivers Saul to Lalo Salamanca as a lawyer the family can use.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The introduction that pulls Saul from petty grift into cartel-scale exposure.

beats.label: S5 · The Domingo play
beats.text: As Saul, Jimmy engineers a plea that flips Domingo into a DEA informant naming Gus's dead drops — Lalo's move, which Gus quietly permits to protect Nacho.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The first move in the Lalo vs Gus war and the first sign Gus knows Lalo is dangerous.

beats.label: S5 · The Acker con
beats.text: Kim rejects Mesa Verde's plan to bulldoze Everett Acker's land; she and Jimmy team up as Saul to extort Kevin Wachtell into a settlement.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kim discovers she likes running cons with Jimmy — the psychological turn behind her Howard proposal.

beats.label: S5 · The wedding
beats.text: Rattled and thrilled by the con, Kim proposes marriage; she and Jimmy wed for spousal privilege as much as anything.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Legally binds them and cements the shared-crime path Kim is now on.

beats.label: S5 · Bagman
beats.text: Lalo is jailed for the Fred killing; Saul carries $7M cash across the desert to bail him out, is ambushed, and only survives because Mike is sent to shoot the ambushers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The trauma that changes Jimmy for good and puts Kim on notice about what Saul work really is.

beats.label: S5 · Kim faces Lalo
beats.text: Lalo comes to Kim's apartment to test their story; Kim faces him down. Convinced enough to leave, Lalo drives for Mexico while Gus arranges a hit on his Chihuahua estate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kim's decisive moment against Lalo, and the setup for the hit that appears to end him.

beats.label: S5 · The open gate
beats.text: Nacho opens Lalo's back gate and flees; Lalo kills every attacker but one and forces him to report Lalo dead. Kim tells Jimmy she wants to destroy Howard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's two live wires for next year — a vengeful Lalo the world thinks is gone, and Kim's Howard plan.

cliffhanger.text: Lalo is alive and reported dead — free to plan a return against Gus. Kim has quit her firm and pitched a con to destroy Howard Hamlin's reputation that Jimmy is not sure he wants to run.
questions: When Lalo reappears, who does he come for first?
Can Nacho survive the fallout of Lalo's 'death'?
How far will Kim go against Howard, and what will it cost them?

characters.name: Jimmy 'Saul Goodman' McGill
characters.line: Now practicing as Saul, he takes on Lalo as a client, marries Kim, and barely survives a desert bail run for the cartel.

characters.name: Kim Wexler
characters.line: Increasingly hooked on the con, she rejects Mesa Verde's tactics on Acker, marries Jimmy, faces down Lalo in her apartment, and tells Jimmy she wants Howard destroyed.

characters.name: Lalo Salamanca
characters.line: The Salamancas' new field commander, jailed and bailed on the Fred killing, who survives Gus's Chihuahua hit and lets the cartel believe him dead.

characters.name: Gus Fring
characters.line: Playing both sides, he lets Lalo's DEA gambit through to protect Nacho and orchestrates the failed assassination on Lalo's estate.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: Gus's fixer, dispatched to shadow Saul's cash run and pick off the ambushers who nearly kill him in the desert.

characters.name: Nacho Varga
characters.line: Gus's mole inside the Salamancas, he opens Lalo's back gate for the hit team and flees into the night.

beats.label: S6 · Nacho's exit
beats.text: Nacho, trapped between Gus and the Salamancas, surrenders in exchange for his father's safety and shoots himself in front of Hector to protect them both.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Nacho's arc and removes Gus's inside man, forcing him into the open against Lalo.

beats.label: S6 · The Howard con
beats.text: Jimmy and Kim run their long con on Howard: fake cocaine, a drugged photo shoot, and an actor impersonating the Sandpiper mediator to force a low settlement.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's moral engine — the cruelty that Kim will finally have to face herself over.

beats.label: S6 · Lalo in Germany
beats.text: Lalo pieces together Gus's superlab from Werner's widow and crew in Germany, then quietly stakes out the laundry above it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The return of the season's antagonist with the proof he needs against Gus.

beats.label: S6 · Howard dies
beats.text: Lalo baits Gus into pulling security off Jimmy and Kim; Howard walks in on their argument and Lalo shoots him dead in their apartment.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The catastrophe that ends Kim's tolerance of her own choices.

beats.label: S6 · Lalo dies
beats.text: Gus lures Lalo into the unfinished lab and kills him with a hidden gun; Mike buries Lalo and Howard together under the lab floor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the cartel war and hides Howard's death under the lab that will define the world beyond this show.

beats.label: S6 · Kim leaves
beats.text: Kim writes an affidavit for Cheryl Hamlin, gives up her law license, and leaves Jimmy — who dives fully into being Saul Goodman.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The break that produces the Saul of the Cadillac and the mansion.

beats.label: S6 · Gene falls
beats.text: Years later, 'Gene' in Omaha is unmasked by Marion via her Life Alert; extradited, Saul discards a plea to bring Kim to court and confesses, including his role in Chuck's death.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final choice — Jimmy reclaims his name and pays the price on purpose.

cliffhanger.text: Jimmy is serving 86 years and has reclaimed both his name and the blame for Chuck. Kim, having confessed her own role, walks free but ruined. The last image is the two of them sharing a cigarette through the prison fence.
questions: What does a life outside the law look like for Kim now?
Does Jimmy find any peace as the man Chuck once told him he could be?
Who is left to hold the world Gus built once the story ends?

characters.name: Jimmy McGill
characters.line: Fully Saul Goodman after Kim leaves, he is finally caught as 'Gene' in Omaha and throws away his plea deal in court to confess everything, including his part in Chuck's death.

characters.name: Kim Wexler
characters.line: The architect of the Howard con, she surrenders her law license and writes Cheryl an affidavit before walking away from Jimmy.

characters.name: Lalo Salamanca
characters.line: Back from the dead, he traces Gus's lab through Werner's widow, shoots Howard in Jimmy and Kim's apartment, and dies in the unfinished superlab.

characters.name: Gus Fring
characters.line: Lures Lalo into the half-built lab and kills him with a hidden pistol, burying the last Salamanca threat under concrete.

characters.name: Howard Hamlin
characters.line: Framed as a cocaine-addled wreck by Jimmy and Kim's con, then shot dead by Lalo the same night and buried beneath the lab.

characters.name: Mike Ehrmantraut
characters.line: Gus's cleaner, who buries Lalo and Howard together under the superlab floor.

characters.name: Saul Goodman
characters.line: The strip-mall persona Jimmy fully becomes once Kim leaves, running a criminal law mill until his Omaha exile as 'Gene'.

characters.name: Marion
characters.line: Gene's kindly Omaha acquaintance who recognises him from a Better Call Saul clip and calls the police from her Life Alert.
